damageIntro.heading: Kerbed it? Cracked it? Hit a pothole?
paragraphs: Most wheel damage falls into one of these. If yours looks like any of them, there's a good chance we can put it right.

damage.title: Kerb & Gutter Rash
damage.summary: The scraped, torn alloy along the rim edge that shows up every time you park.

damage.title: Buckles & Bends
damage.summary: A rim knocked out of round by a pothole. You'll feel it as a wobble through the wheel.

damage.title: Cracks
damage.summary: A split in the rim, usually after a solid impact. Often repairable, depending where it sits.

damage.title: Corrosion & Lacquer Peel
damage.summary: That milky, flaking finish creeping out from a chip in the clear coat.

damage.title: Diamond-Cut Face Damage
damage.summary: Machined-face wheels that have lost their shine or copped a kerb across the front.

damage.title: Tired or Wrong Colour
damage.summary: Wheels that are structurally fine but just don't suit the car any more.

resultBlock.heading: Off the lathe, onto the car
paragraphs: This is what a diamond-cut finish actually is: fine concentric lines cut into bare aluminium by the lathe, sealed under fresh lacquer. It catches the light in a way no paint or polish can imitate.

That's why a machined-face wheel has to go back on a lathe to be put right. There's no hand-finishing your way to it — the geometry has to be *cut*, and cut to the profile that wheel left the factory with.

newcomer.heading: New to the Highlands. Not new to the work.
paragraphs: Until now, getting a wheel properly machined around here meant packing it off to Wollongong or Sydney, paying for the freight, and waiting on a courier both ways.
So we brought the machine to Bowral instead.

Our CNC lathe is installed and cutting at Mount Road — not a partner's machine somewhere down the highway, not a job we quietly send out and mark up. When we say the work is done in-house, we mean in *this* house.

We're the new name in Southern Highlands wheel repair, and we're setting out to be the one people recommend. The plan for getting there isn't complicated: do proper work, give straight answers, and hand back wheels people are pleased to put back on the car.
Bring us something kerbed, buckled or cracked and let us show you.

straightAnswers.heading: We'll tell you if it's not worth it
paragraphs: Here's something you won't read on many wheel repair websites: not every wheel can be saved. Funny how everyone else's site implies anything can be fixed, isn't it?

Cracks in the spokes are a hard no — and not because we can't be bothered. The spokes carry every bit of your cornering and braking load, so welding them isn't just risky, it's not legal. Rim lip cracks are usually a different story and often perfectly repairable.
Diamond-cut wheels are similar. Every re-cut takes a whisker of metal off the face, so there's a limit to how many times one wheel can go under the tool. We'll tell you where yours is at.
You'll get a straight answer either way. Sometimes that answer is "replace it" — and we'd rather say so than take your money and hand back something we're not proud of.

workshop.heading: The machine that does the work
paragraphs: This is our CNC wheel lathe, installed at Mount Road in Bowral. A wheel is chucked on the spindle, measured, and the cutting tool follows the exact face profile that wheel was built with — restoring the finish rather than approximating it.

It is the reason we can say the machining happens here. A lot of places advertise diamond cutting and quietly courier your wheels to someone else's lathe, then add the freight and the waiting to your bill. Ours is twenty metres from the front counter.
Around it sits the rest of what a wheel needs: a straightening press, TIG welding gear, a blasting and prep bay, and a spray booth with oven curing.

services.title: CNC Diamond-Cut Refinishing
services.summary: Machined-face wheels re-cut on the lathe to restore the original finish.
services.what: A diamond-cut finish is made by a lathe skimming bare aluminium to leave fine concentric cut lines under a coat of lacquer. It is a machined surface, not a paint effect.
services.fixes: Kerb damage across the machined face, lacquer peel, and the milky corrosion that creeps under a chipped clear coat.
services.how: The wheel is mounted on our CNC lathe and the face is cut back to the model's original profile, then re-lacquered. Hand polishing cannot reproduce that geometry — it has to be cut. Every re-cut removes a little metal, so there is a limit to how many times one wheel can go under the tool, and we'll tell you where yours sits.

services.title: Wheel Straightening
services.summary: Buckles and flat spots corrected and trued.
services.what: Hydraulic correction of a rim bent out of round, usually after a pothole or a hard kerb strike.
services.fixes: The vibration and wobble that appears through the steering or the seat once a rim is no longer running true.
services.how: The wheel is measured for runout, heated and pressed back true, then re-checked on the machine to confirm it runs straight before anything else happens to it.

services.title: Crack & Weld Repair
services.summary: Repairable cracks TIG welded, dressed and refinished.
services.what: Aluminium TIG welding of a cracked rim, followed by dressing the weld back to the original profile.
services.fixes: Cracks on the back or the middle of the rim lip, which is where impact damage usually shows up.
services.how: The crack is ground out, welded, dressed and refinished. Cracks through a spoke are the exception: the spokes carry your cornering and braking loads, and repairing them is not legal. We'll tell you straight if that's what you've got.

services.title: Full Refurbishment
services.summary: Stripped back and rebuilt to a factory-quality finish.
services.what: A complete strip, repair and refinish — one wheel, or a full set brought back to matching condition.
services.fixes: Tired, oxidised, peeling or mismatched wheels that let an otherwise tidy car down.
services.how: Tyres off, weights and TPMS sensors removed and set aside, old finish stripped, damage repaired, then primed, coloured, cleared and oven cured.

services.title: Colour Changes & Custom Finishes
services.summary: Gloss, satin, matte, two-tone or machined face with an accent.
services.what: A full change of finish rather than a restoration of the original colour.
services.fixes: Wheels that are structurally sound but wrong for the car — or just due for something different.
services.how: We match OEM colours where you want factory-correct, or work to whatever finish you're after. Two-tone and machined-face-with-accent combinations are cut on the lathe, which is what gives them a clean edge.

services.title: Gutter Rash & Kerb Damage
services.summary: The scuffed lip and face made good again.
services.what: Cosmetic repair of the outer lip and face after contact with a kerb or a gutter.
services.fixes: The scraped, torn alloy along the rim edge that catches your eye every time you walk up to the car.
services.how: Damage is filled or machined back depending on how deep it runs, then refinished to match the rest of the wheel.

services.title: TPMS Handling
services.summary: Tyre pressure sensors removed, protected and refitted properly.
services.what: Proper care of the tyre pressure monitoring sensors fitted inside most modern wheels.
services.fixes: The dashboard warning light that turns up after a careless wheel refit — and the cost of replacing a sensor that was blasted or painted over.
services.how: Sensors come out before stripping, stay clear of blasting and paint, then go back in or get transferred and reset when the wheel returns to the car.

process.title: Assessment
process.summary: We look at the wheel properly before quoting.
process.detail: The wheel is inspected for runout, cracks and previous repairs. If it isn't worth repairing, or isn't safe to repair, we say so at this point rather than after you've paid.

media.alt: A wheel being inspected on the bench
media.shotNeeded: Wheel being measured or inspected on the bench

process.title: Tyre Removal & Strip
process.detail: Tyre off, balance weights and TPMS sensor removed and set aside, then the old finish stripped so we can see exactly what we're working with instead of guessing through the paint.

process.title: Straightening
process.summary: Bends and buckles pressed back true.
process.detail: Buckles and flat spots are corrected hydraulically, then the wheel is re-measured to confirm it runs true. There's no point machining a face on a rim that's still out of round.

media.alt: A wheel being straightened on the press

process.title: Welding
process.detail: Cracks on the back or middle of the rim are ground out, TIG welded and dressed back to profile. Spoke cracks are not repaired — that's a structural limit, not a preference.

media.shotNeeded: TIG welding in progress on a rim

process.title: CNC Machining
process.summary: The face cut back to its original profile.
process.detail: The wheel is chucked on the lathe and the face is machined to the model's original profile, restoring the fine concentric cut lines that make a diamond-cut finish what it is. This is the step most shops around here have to send away.

media.alt: A wheel being machined on our CNC lathe

process.title: Finishing
process.detail: Primer, colour and clear coat go on in the booth and are oven cured, which is what gives the finish the hardness to cope with Highlands weather and winter road grit.

media.alt: A wheel in the spray booth
media.shotNeeded: Wheel in the booth being sprayed

process.title: Balance & Refit
process.summary: Back on the car, balanced and torqued.
process.detail: Tyre refitted, the wheel balanced, TPMS sensor refitted and reset, and every nut torqued to the manufacturer's specification. You drive away with it done properly, not nearly done.

story.heading: Wheel repair, done in the Highlands
paragraphs: Bowral Wheel Repairs exists for a simple reason: there was no CNC wheel lathe in the Southern Highlands, and every machined wheel in the district was being trucked somewhere else to get fixed.
We do one thing and we do it here — alloy wheels, straightened, welded, machined and refinished at Mount Road in Bowral.
That focus is deliberate. A wheel is a structural part holding a tonne and a half of car onto the road, and it deserves more than being a sideline to something else.

intro.heading: Tell us what you've done to it
paragraphs: Send through a photo and a few details and we'll tell you what your wheels need. Or just call — we'd rather talk it through than trade emails.
